_why: `stage()` measured nothing while `h_mad_assemble_audit` held size guards one file over. The FIRST fix was wrong in the permissive direction and its own tests defended the wrong boundary: it reused `prompt_oversize`, which counts CHARACTERS against codex's stdin limit, while `exec agy` passes the prompt as ONE argv element bounded by ARG_MAX -- a BYTE budget the kernel shares with envp. Measured: an argv payload at the old character limit fails `OSError 7 Argument list too long`, and 1037859 B succeeds. Reusing a measured constant imported the other surface's UNITS with its number. Each mutation carries its own `test` key; two of them are the exact directions a fresh review caught.

mutations.name: the-budget-ignores-the-environment-it-shares-ARG_MAX-with
mutations._mechanism: Restores the defect a fresh review found. Dropping the env and argv reserve puts the budget back at ~ARG_MAX, and the kernel refuses the largest payload the gate then blesses -- the staged prompt is undeliverable and the operator reads the E2BIG as '6a-prime failed'.

mutations.name: the-gate-counts-characters-again
mutations._mechanism: The unit, isolated. Every ASCII fixture in this file passes either way, which is exactly why the character version shipped -- only multi-byte content separates them, and the designs this channel inlines measure 1.004-1.010 bytes/char.

mutations.name: the-size-gate-never-fires
mutations._mechanism: The state before any of this. A prompt no surface accepts is written to disk and reported STAGED; the operator dispatches it and reads the refusal as a failed review.
mutations.find:
if oversize:
        # Writing no file is not the same as leaving no file.
mutations.replace:
if False:
        # Writing no file is not the same as leaving no file.

mutations.name: the-gate-measures-the-body-before-the-contract-prepend
mutations._mechanism: The placement, isolated from the gate's existence. Discounting the contract's ~800 bytes passes a prompt deliverable only until the contract is added -- the original defect with a size check bolted on that cannot see the last thing written.
mutations.replace: oversize, size, budget, reserve = _size_gate(body[len(contract_head):] if report_file is not None else body)

mutations.name: the-oversize-prompt-is-written-anyway
mutations._mechanism: Halting but leaving the file is worse than not halting: the next copy-pasted dispatch line finds a prompt on disk and sends it. A test asserting only the token would pass here.

mutations.name: the-halt-does-not-name-its-escape-hatch
mutations._mechanism: A halt whose remedy is unstated is a wall: the operator's visible options become shrinking the design by hand or abandoning 6a-prime, and --vh-tail goes unused.
mutations.find: "Re-run with --vh-tail N to inline only the last N Version History "

mutations.name: vh-tail-is-parsed-but-never-reaches-stage
mutations._mechanism: The flag appears in --help, argparse accepts it, and it silently does nothing -- a documented remedy that looks implemented. The prompt comes back the same size and the operator concludes the design is irreducible.

mutations.name: the-trim-keeps-every-entry
mutations._mechanism: The delegation itself, at the other end from the wiring mutation. Both produce an unchanged prompt, so each needs its own kill.

mutations.name: the-stale-prompt-survives-the-halt
mutations._mechanism: The hole the first version of this gate had. 6a-prime iterates against ONE --prompt path and cycle N's dispatch line stays in scrollback, so leaving the superseded prompt on disk means re-running that line reviews the OLD prompt and comes back clean -- while the comment claims an unwritten prompt cannot be dispatched by mistake.

mutations.name: the-halt-removes-the-prompt-silently
mutations._mechanism: A file disappearing without a word is worse than one that stays: the operator cannot tell a halt that cleared a superseded prompt from one that never wrote anything, and will not know the scrollback command is now dead.

mutations.name: stale_removed-is-a-constant-not-a-measurement
mutations._mechanism: Reporting 1 unconditionally makes the field decorative: it would claim a removal on a path that was already clear, and a reader who trusts it stops checking.

mutations.name: the-audit-template-stops-asking-for-the-done-marker
mutations._mechanism: The producer half of the contract that makes `failure-recovery.md`'s phase split correct. Edit this sentence out and phases 3/4/5b's bare `report-wait` hangs exactly as 6a-prime's did, with nothing to say so -- the review that found this called the sentence load-bearing and unpinned.
